summary.text: A 49-year-old male presented on May 3, 2023, with no significant medical, personal or familial history. Examination showed diffuse infiltrated plaques and papulonodular lesions, widespread sterile pustules on an erythematous base, large yellowish plaques with pustules on the soles and nail changes, with PASI 22 and DLQI 27. The authors judged the picture highly suggestive of a generalized pustular psoriasis flare complicating plaque-type psoriasis.

Laboratory results included glucose, insulin, C-peptide and lipid values, elevated CRP, ALT 58 U/L, and negative diabetes-related autoantibodies; the text HbA1c of 7.8% and the AST value differ from Table 1. Skin biopsy confirmed psoriasis and abdominal ultrasound revealed severe MASLD, and T2DM, psoriasis and MASLD were diagnosed. Initial acitretin, topical tretinoin, sodium thiosulfate and metformin gave no significant improvement and psoriasis progressed rapidly.

Semaglutide 0.25 mg/week was started on May 17, 2023, designated Baseline, with continued metformin 1,000 mg daily, discontinuation of acitretin and other medications, and maintained topical tretinoin. The dose was escalated to 0.5 mg/week after 4 weeks and 1 mg/week at 8 weeks. Mild transient nausea occurred during escalation without vomiting, and no antiemetics were required.

At Week 12, weight loss was 4 kg with gradual pustule resolution, plaque shrinkage and improved pruritus. At Week 24 the body weight was reduced by 6 kg, PASI was 6.2, psoriatic lesions and pruritus showed near-complete resolution and ultrasound showed reduced hepatic steatosis. The regimen was well tolerated without hypoglycemia or severe adverse events, and the patient remains on semaglutide with a planned 1-year follow-up.
